newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, March 15 Initial Claims from 312,000, March 15 4-Week Average from 312,250, March 8 Continued Claims from 2,328,000 and March 1 from 2,327,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 313,000 in the March 22 week.
Continued claims in the week ended March 15 were at their lowest level since the week ended Dec 9, 1989, when they hit 2,268,000, the department said.
Labor said four states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended March 15, the latest period for which data are available.
They were California, with 5,891 fewer new filings; Pennsylvania, with 2,275; New York, with 1,950; and Ohio, with 1,793.
Pennsylvania reported fewer layoffs in the primary metals, paper, furniture, and lumber and wood industries. The other states had no comment.
Three states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 in the March 15 week.
They were Arkansas, with 1,528 additional new filings; Tennessee, with 1,319; and North Carolina, with 1,157.

Arkansas said it had layoffs in the trade industry. Tennessee reported layoffs in the food, textile, apparel, furniture, scientific instruments, trade and service industries. North Carolina gave no reason for the increase.
